No conclusion is made that the prescribed 6 km work distance was completed or missed.
No causal attribution of slower late-work speed to wind is made.

limitations: The cause of the clock disagreement is unknown.
claims.statement: The SpeedCoach and mobile recordings describe the same outing, with a preserved 37-second clock offset.

limitations: Reconstruction is based on SpeedCoach stroke-rate classification.
claims.statement: Six work intervals were reconstructed, matching the six planned repetitions; no planned work interval was missing.
All five reconstructed intervening recoveries lasted 240 seconds, within the prescribed 180–300 second range.

limitations: Speed change alone does not establish athlete improvement, regression, or cause.
claims.statement: Work speed was higher in work-04 (3.459 m/s) than in work-05 (2.970 m/s) and work-06 (3.168 m/s); work-05 also had a lower average rate (19.99 SPM) than its prescribed range.

limitations: Segment distances are boundary-derived from SPM classification, exclude transitions, and cannot be summed to assess prescribed-distance completion.
claims.statement: Completion or shortfall of the prescribed 6 km work distance cannot be determined from reconstructed segment distances.
Use during the first block and removal before the second block of the prescribed resistance band are unknown.

limitations: No coach observation or perceived-effort report was supplied; telemetry cannot establish these attributes.
claims.statement: Technique, crew synchronization, and perceived effort are unknown.

coach_briefing: The six planned work efforts and all five recoveries were reconstructed. Stroke-rate targets were met in work-01 through work-04 and work-06; work-05 averaged 19.99 SPM, below its 22–24 SPM target. Late-work speed was lower while the wind shifted from tailwind to substantial headwind, an association rather than a proven cause. Confirm band use and the reason for the fifth-repetition rate reduction; do not judge prescribed-distance completion from the reconstructed segment distances.

deviations.description: Average stroke rate was 19.99 SPM, below the prescribed 22–24 SPM range for the final three work repetitions.

limitations: Wind timing and speed cannot establish that wind caused the observed speed changes or athlete regression.
environment_assessment.summary: Conditions shifted from a 1.0 m/s effective tailwind at session start to a 5.5 m/s effective headwind by the end; the effective-headwind sign changed at 1,800 s and gusts ranged from 1.3 to 7.0 m/s. This timing overlaps the late work intervals and supports an association with their speed changes, not causation.

follow_up_questions: Was the resistance band used for work-01 through work-03 and removed before work-04?
Was there any operational reason for lowering the stroke rate during work-05?
What was the crew's perceived effort during the late headwind portion?

prescribed_blocks: 3 × 1 km at 19–21 SPM with resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery
3 × 1 km at 22–24 SPM without resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery
plan_summary.summary: Plan: six 1 km work repetitions—first three at 19–21 SPM with a resistance band, final three at 22–24 SPM without it—with 180–300 s active recoveries. Six work intervals and five intervening recoveries were reconstructed; prescribed-distance completion remains insufficient.

session_associations.reason: Bidirectional route overlap supports one outing despite the mobile record starting 37 seconds later.

source_policy.reason: SpeedCoach reports SPM; mobile SPM is entirely zero and is rejected.
Mobile cumulative distance has a supplied bias/conflict flag and ends 1.2% higher; sources were not averaged.
Only SpeedCoach supplies usable speed windows; mobile provides no speed series.
SpeedCoach route is corroborated by close bidirectional mobile-route overlap.
Time-aligned environmental series supplies wind conditions; it is used for association only.
